chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Muskhan from Sulayman ibn Khalid from one of them, who said:
When Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who died leaving behind a slave-wife, he said: He buys her from his estate, frees her, and then she inherits.

key_terms.امْرَأَةٌ مَمْلُوكَةٌ: Slave-wife (a female slave owned by her husband)
key_terms.وَرَّثَهَا: He made her inherit / She inherits

ai.seo_question: What happens to a slave-wife when her master husband dies according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific mechanism of *itq* (manumission) for a slave-wife, emphasizing that her freedom is funded from the deceased husband's estate rather than being automatic. This ruling ensures her transition to free status, thereby granting her the right to inherit as a wife, a principle highly valued in Shia jurisprudence for protecting the financial security of women in mixed-status marriages.
